title: LR4 crossover — complementary serial tree, smooth interpolation
description:
Implement the four-zone LR4 multiband crossover as a complementary serial tree with click-free crossover motion and ordering protection per SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §5.3 and §21.4.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Before editing, inspect:
- .abracapocus/SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §5.2–5.3 (zones, LR4 definition, crossover defaults/ranges)
- .abracapocus/SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §21.4 (reconstruction: flat magnitude when all zones unity; tolerance-based, not sample-identical)
- Source/DSP/BiquadCoefficients.h/.cpp for Butterworth/LP/HP SOS builders (read only)
- Source/DSP/TPTFilter.* and sibling DSP prepare/reset/process style (read only)
- Source/ParameterIDs.h multiband crossover IDs if present (read only; do not edit)

Implement Source/DSP/MultibandCrossover.h and Source/DSP/MultibandCrossover.cpp:
1. MultibandCrossover class with prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize), reset(), and process that splits mono or multi-channel input into four zone buffers (Weight, Body, Bite, Fizz/Air) without heap in the process path.
2. Each LR4 stage is two cascaded second-order Butterworth sections (Q = 1/sqrt(2)): H_LR4_LP = H_BW2_LP^2, H_LR4_HP = H_BW2_HP^2. Prefer reusing BiquadCoefficients (or equivalent project SOS) rather than inventing a new filter framework.
3. Complementary serial tree: cascade split points so bypassed/unity zone recombination reconstructs input with flat magnitude response (phase may be frequency-dependent; do not require sample-identical dry copies).
4. Three crossovers with defaults and clamp ranges: Weight/Body 140 Hz (40–500), Body/Bite 900 Hz (150–3000), Bite/Fizz 4500 Hz (1000–12000). Provide setters that smoothly interpolate target frequencies (zipper/click-free motion).
5. Ordering protection: enforce f1 < f2 < f3 with a small guard gap when automation would cross or collide; never allow inverted bands.
6. Expose zone buffer access or an API MultibandEngine can call to split into four bands and later recombine (recombine may live here as sum of zone outputs, or document that Engine sums — prefer a clear sumZones or processSplit API).
7. Optional getters for effective/smoothed crossover Hz for GUI and tests.

Do NOT edit MultibandZone, MultibandEngine, PluginProcessor, CMakeLists.txt, or tests.
acceptance_criteria: MultibandCrossover implements LR4 splits as cascaded Butterworth pairs (Q=1/sqrt(2)) in a complementary serial tree into four zones
Crossover defaults/ranges match Weight/Body 140 Hz (40–500), Body/Bite 900 Hz (150–3000), Bite/Fizz 4500 Hz (1000–12000) with smooth interpolation and f1<f2<f3 ordering protection
Unity-gain recombination API yields flat magnitude reconstruction intent (documented/tolerance-friendly; not sample-identical)
No heap allocation in per-sample or per-block process paths
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/BiquadCoefficients.* or Source/DSP/TPTFilter.* beyond include/use
implement MultibandZone dynamics or PluginProcessor wiring

allowed: reuse BiquadCoefficients Butterworth/LP/HP SOS for LR4 pairs
float buffer API matching sibling DSP modules
own internal zone scratch buffers sized at prepare
minimum frequency guard gap for ordering protection
forbidden: GUI paint or APVTS layout ownership
require sample-identical reconstruction tests in this task
